preconditions.description: Attacker must have some balance of the target token to initiate transfer
Contract must not be paused (paused == false)
Attacker must not be blacklisted (isBlackListed[attacker] == false)

exploit_hint: The contract's transfer function has a fee calculation bug where it subtracts the full _value from sender's balance but only adds (value - fee) to recipient. However, the owner receives the fee separately. This creates a discrepancy but doesn't directly increase attacker balance. The real exploit is that the contract doesn't properly handle ERC20 return values - it doesn't check return value of transferFrom in the upgraded contract. If deprecated=true and upgradedAddress points to a malicious contract that doesn't transfer tokens but returns success, attackers can drain funds. First, become owner (or wait for owner to deprecate to a malicious contract), then call transfer/transferFrom to move tokens without actual transfer.
